# Work Simulation & Work Style Assessment

[← Amazon](../README.md) · [Every Amazon question](../../amazon.md) · [Read it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/study/work-style-simulation-assessment)

`work-style`

---

## What it includes

- The non-programming section of the SDE OA consists of two computer-scored assessments:
  - **Work Simulation** — workplace-judgment situations arranged into modules, such as "Project Alert / API design, feedback and debugging" and "Sound Traveller / tracking-platform decision." Each scenario presents a work situation with multiple possible replies; score every reply from 1 to 5 for effectiveness (1 = least effective, 5 = most effective).
  - **Work Style** — approximately 35 paired, forced-choice questions; for every pair, select which statement describes you more closely using the Most-like / More-like scale running from the left choice to the right choice.

## Illustrations

- Work Simulation (Project Alert module): a senior developer gives review comments that are more complicated to implement but provide lasting benefit; you assess responses such as *"Could we meet to go over your concerns and suggestions?"* and *"You are welcome to modify the code however you believe is appropriate."*
- Work Style item: *"I prefer roles that let me develop unfamiliar abilities"* <----> *"I learn something new when I already know I can use it immediately."*

## Notes

- Work Simulation favors conduct consistent with Amazon Leadership Principles: receive criticism constructively, investigate problems with ownership, seek assistance early, do not brush aside a senior engineer's concern, and escalate by suggesting a meeting instead of making a solo decision or delaying the release.
- Pay close attention to the rating scale's direction — on each screen, 1 means least effective and 5 means most effective; time pressure makes it easy to reverse them.
- Work Style provides no publicly available answer key and is scored for consistency. Since both choices are generally positive, respond truthfully and preserve the same view of yourself across repeated themes (planning versus adapting, checking details versus taking initiative, and learning versus carrying out work) instead of trying to maximize one question.

## Preparation

- Connect every Leadership Principle with its corresponding "most effective" action (ownership, earning trust, diving deep, bias for action, and escalating with a plan) so the Work Simulation decisions become straightforward.
- Before beginning Work Style, decide where you consistently fall on the recurring dimensions (planner versus adapter, detail verifier versus initiator) so differently worded versions remain aligned.
